summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of poorly controlled type 1 diabetes, hypertension, depression, and alcohol abuse was admitted for hyperglycemia and a urinary tract infection. She presented with nausea, vomiting, and a blood glucose of 505 but no evidence of ketoacidosis. Urinalysis showed significant white blood cells, and culture confirmed pan-sensitive E. coli. She was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and transitioned to oral Bactrim for a five-day course. Her insulin regimen was intensified due to infection-related insulin resistance, increasing her Lantus dose from 25 to 30 units and adjusting mealtime Humalog doses. Her blood sugars stabilized, and she remained asymptomatic from a cardiac and psychiatric standpoint. She reported one month of sobriety supported by sertraline and naltrexone. She was discharged home with updated insulin instructions, completion of antibiotics, and close follow-up with her primary care provider and endocrinologist.
